extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH R01-style grant applications and molecular microbiology researchers performing protein–DNA binding site selection (SELEX/PCR-ABS)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH R01 grant application in microbiology
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and peer-review of an NIH R01 research proposal focused on identifying transcription factor binding sites (SarA) and downstream regulatory targets in Staphylococcus aureus, including detailed experimental methods (PCR-ABS/SELEX, EMSA, cloning, sequencing, Northern blot confirmation).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCR-ABS primer end-design requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The 70-mer includes defined 20 bp sites at each end; the only requirements for the design of these defined sites are 1) that they have no obvious similarity to the binding site of interest and 2) that they are distinct by comparison to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design 20 bp termini such that they do not contain any form of the agr heptads (AGTTAAG, AGTTAGG, CTTAACT, CCTAACT) or any sequence longer than a few base pairs (~5–6) matching upstream of cna. The two 20 bp sites must be unique relative to each other to avoid primer annealing between primer sites (since PCR generates random sequence between them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target region length for PCR-ABS
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 30 bp randomized target region for the first round of experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection based on prior data suggesting SarA binds within a ~28 bp region; a 30 bp region is chosen to encompass potential binding variability. The sequence within the 30 bp randomized region is intentionally random for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of PCR amplifications to generate randomized pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplification of the 70 bp fragment is done using an equimolar mixture of all four nucleotides so that the central 30 bp region has a random sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize three oligonucleotides (70-mer with 20 bp defined ends + two primers). Use primer 2 for initial extension to generate double-stranded DNA, then both primers to amplify with equimolar dNTPs and include [(32)P]dCTP for labeling where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain complexity of starting DNA pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 40–50 µg of synthetic template for a single round of primer extension to generate the starting DNA and maintain complexity of the fragment pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large amounts of template reduce loss of diversity in early cycles of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection cycle parameters (binding, purification, amplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic PCR-ABS protocol steps: 1) amplification of a pool of fragments containing randomized sequences, 2) EMSA experiments for binding, 3) purification of bound fragments, 4) cloning and sequencing of selected fragments; repeat binding/purification/amplification cycles ~5–7 times to enhance selectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep number of PCR cycles relatively low (~14–20) in each amplification to avoid nucleotide depletion and artifactual PCR products. Monitor enrichment by EMSA; the fraction of bound DNAs should increase until a steady state level is achieved, which helps decide when to stop cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for separating bound and unbound DNAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Two methods: (a) immunoprecipitation using affinity-purified SarA antibody and protein A–sepharose to pull down bound DNAs; (b) EMSA followed by visualization and excision of bound fraction from gel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After immunoprecipitation, elute DNAs, purify by phenol/chloroform extraction and ethanol precipitation. For EMSA, visualize by autoradiography, excise, elute, then phenol/chloroform extract and precipitate. When using immunoprecipitation, also do EMSA with both bound and unbound fragments to check product size and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cloning strategy to minimize bias and facilitate throughput
rubrics_metrics.description: Clone enriched DNAs by blunt-end cloning into a SmaI site and use restriction sites engineered into the 20 bp flanking regions to facilitate generation of multiple clones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 20 bp primers include three restriction sites to help cloning. Use blunt-end cloning to minimize bias associated with removing fragments that contain restriction sites; use flanking restriction sites to speed multiple-clone generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing sample size and consensus derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence approximately 100–150 cloned DNAs and align sequences (PILEUP) to derive a consensus SarA-binding site based on relative nucleotide abundance at each position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align the 30 bp regions and define the consensus as the most likely base at each position across the entire target region. An example alignment and percentage representation at each position should be used to call consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing specificity and contribution of individual bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange selected sequences on a homology gradient from most to least similar to consensus; pick representative DNAs (high, moderate, low homology) and determine equilibrium dissociation constants by quantitative EMSA. Test single-base changes implicated as important by abundance data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pairs of fragments differing by a single base at implicated positions. For quantitative EMSA, use limiting 32P-labeled DNA (<10 pM), equilibrate with various SarA concentrations, run native gels, fix/dry/expose to X-ray film, use laser densitometry to quantify unbound DNA, calculate bound DNA by subtraction, plot bound vs protein concentration, and derive apparent KD at 50% complex formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EMSA and densitometry for KD estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quantitative EMSA and laser densitometry to quantitate bound and unbound DNA and derive apparent KD values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure details: limiting labeled DNA (<10 pM), range of protein concentrations, native gel electrophoresis, densitometry of unbound band, bound = total − unbound. Determine protein concentration giving 50% complex formation as apparent KD. This approach was validated in prior studies cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genome searching criteria for putative binding sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the consensus SarA-binding site to search the S. aureus genomic database (FASTA in GCG) with degenerate parameters based on PCR-ABS results and include architectural parameters that affect affinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make search parameters degenerate at positions showing no clear base preference; include spacing/architectural features such as spacing of heptanucleotide repeats. Consider a putative site likely only if it is cis to known or reasonable promoters; identify genes cis to these promoters for follow-up testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of sar-mediated regulation by Northern blot
rubrics_metrics.description: Test candidate genes for sar-mediated regulation by Northern blots using total cellular RNA from wild-type strains and their corresponding sar mutants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolate RNA at various growth stages (e.g., exponential and post-exponential) to ensure regulatory effects are detected. Use PCR-generated DNA probes; standard Northern protocols described elsewhere in the proposal apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and cross-checks in selection protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform EMSA with both bound and unbound DNA fractions even when using immunoprecipitation to ensure appropriate product size and consistency; check that fraction of bound DNAs increases to steady state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that size of amplification product (unbound fraction) is appropriate and that bound fraction size remains relatively constant. Use these checks to validate selection specificity and to monitor enrichment across cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCR cycle number guidance to avoid artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep number of PCR cycles relatively low (~14–20) during amplifications to avoid nucleotide depletion and generation of artifactual PCR products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive cycles can skew pool composition and introduce artifacts that invalidate selection/enrichment results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of reference list size and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Less than 100 citations. Includes everything cited in application. More references might indicate lack of focus. Less could indicate insufficient knowledge of field. Titles included in references help readers identify subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reference list length and inclusion of titles as signals: overly long lists may suggest unfocused literature review; very short lists may suggest inadequate familiarity with field. Including titles is helpful for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review criterion — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem and will it further understanding of regulatory switching mechanisms in Staphylococcus aureus relevant to pathogenesis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the hypothesis is well founded on prior studies and whether the proposed work addresses significant gaps (e.g., agr-independent sar regulation, cna control, virulence relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review criterion — Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the experimental design, preliminary results, and methods well articulated and appropriate to test the hypotheses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the clarity of methodology (e.g., purification of SarA, generation of monospecific antiserum, reporter fusion vectors, mutants), adequacy of preliminary data and reagents, and whether methods convincingly address specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review criterion — Investigator and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are investigators well qualified and in possession of necessary molecular expertise and reagents to complete the proposed studies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider PI and Co-I experience, prior success purifying relevant proteins, availability of mutants and reagents, and access to facilities (e.g., automated sequencer, core facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of dependencies on external data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of target genes depends on availability of S. aureus genomic sequence data; ability to pursue experiments will be greatly facilitated as complete genome sequence becomes available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly note dependency and adapt search strategies (degenerate searches) as genomic datasets expand; plan to re-run homology searches when more sequence data becomes public.
